story: Gary is out in his driveway at his house, zip-tying and taping the wiring on his golf cart neatly with the lights off, feeling content about the work. Donna is at her house stretching and warming up with her paddle, eager and watching the corner for Gary so they can start their practice. Over on Magnolia Loop, Hal is on dutiful patrol, counting the pink flamingos he can see from the street so he can report the tally to the review committee. Meanwhile, at her house, Rosa is optimistic about the dinner party, setting out place cards and counting chairs for six while she plans a menu around Hal's cornbread and Donna's lemon bars.
events: Gary (gary golf cart): Zip-tie and tape the wiring runs neat and secure, lights off
Donna waited: Stretching out and warming up with my paddle, watching for Gary to come around the corner for our practice.
Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos visible from the street and note the tally for the review committee
Rosa (rosa dining table): Set out place cards and count chairs for six, planning the menu around Hal's cornbread and Donna's lemon bars

gary.thought_process: The light harness and speaker bracket are mounted, and I did the quiet continuity check last tick. I grabbed zip ties and tape from the toolbox, so now I tidy up the wiring runs. Lights stay off until Thanksgiving per L-04, no amplified sound, and the Architectural Review application is already filed for the street-visible mods. Nobody's around to talk to, so I just get on with the cart. It feels good to be useful, even if it's only for myself.

parameters.content: Zip-tie and tape the wiring runs neat and secure, lights off

donna.thought_process: I've penciled in the court slot, packed the bag, and texted Gary the time. Nothing more to do here and no one's around to talk to. I'm already at the Rec Center, so the sensible thing is to wait for Gary to show up and warm up. Not going to text him again since I just did. Keep it within the two-hour limit under L-05.

parameters.content: Stretching out and warming up with my paddle, watching for Gary to come around the corner for our practice.

hal.thought_process: I'm on Magnolia Loop at 11:17 with nobody around. My recent memories show I've already counted Donna's flamingos this morning and logged it, and I've posted the L-02 and L-01 notice on the bulletin board. Gary has filed his paperwork, so that matter is settled. The flamingo flock is right here in the zone, so I can do an official, street-level count from the public way, which is the only count that matters under L-02. A proper tally from the street, noted for the review committee, keeps this by the book. Saturday at Rosa's is settled, so there's no hurry. Order first, then cornbread.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos visible from the street and note the tally for the review committee

rosa.thought_process: Everyone's committed to Saturday at six: Hal, Gary, and Donna. The invite is pinned on the bulletin board, so there's no one left to chase. I'm home now and nobody's around, so the useful thing is the actual hosting. Six guests means seating and a menu to settle, and it's Friday, so tomorrow I have to be ready. The dining table is the obvious place to start. I can work out the seating around Hal's cornbread and Donna's lemon bars, make sure there are enough chairs, and get a grocery list going before my per-diem shift schedule gets in the way.

parameters.content: Set out place cards and count chairs for six, planning the menu around Hal's cornbread and Donna's lemon bars

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
